events.credibility_reason: The author conceded in the thread on 13 August 2024 that it is 'not a rigorous math proof (yet)' and that it 'still contains a -minor- logical hole': a possible deep forced White win that his argument does not rule out. Every critic said it is not a proof, he ended the discussion, and no later work cites it. The argument rests on empirical engine and database evidence, which cannot exclude a deep forced win.

why: The statement asks for one thing: the value of the starting position. The only event that claims to give it is jefk's August 2024 TalkChess draft, so its claimed scope is whole. I answered it knocked_down rather than doubtful because the author himself conceded that it is not a rigorous proof and named a specific gap in the key step, a possible deep forced win that his argument does not exclude, and he never answered it. That counts as a concession on the central claim. Endgame tablebases (op1, the Syzygy 8-piece generator, and the pre-snapshot tables and records) give exact values for endgame positions, but those values do not bound or settle the value of the start, which has no intermediate quantity, so I answered them none. Romano's preprint gives a search procedure that cannot be run in practice, with conditional theorems, and states no value, so it is none; even a 'named side cannot lose' result would follow from Zermelo-type existence unless the side were identified, and the record cannot identify it. The Seven paper says nothing about chess's value on the abstract, so it is none. Minichess, Losing Chess and infinite chess are variants. No AI system produced mathematics in any event: the May 2024 thread mentions ChatGPT-4 discussions and AlphaZero only as intuition, and its systems list is empty.
doubts: One close call: if Romano's draw-strategy theorem were confirmed to apply to the start for an identified side, it might count as a case (that side cannot lose). The record has this only from a summarising fetch and cannot say which side, so I answered none. The jefk claim's verdict does not depend on whether the knocked_down or not_credible label applies, because both set it aside.
